transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-30
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Marcus (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), David Lin (Orchid Head of Platform), Emily Carter (Procurement), Ravi Shah (Security), Sofia Morales (Legal)
Recording link: https://app.fireflies.ai/recordings/fireflies-20250930-efb7a2 (placeholder)

[00:00] Marcus: Hey everybody, thanks for joining. Marcus from Redwood Inference, AE. With me is Priya from solutions engineering. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] David: Doing well, thanks. Appreciate you taking time. We're trying to move through vendor intake this week so wanted to align on contract risk and the SLAs.
[00:18] Marcus: Great. Quick agenda — MSA/DPA expectations, what security needs, SLA and Dedicated vs hosted economics, and procurement questions. Then next steps. Sound good?
[00:28] Emily: Yep that's what procurement wants. We need to understand pricing bands and who owns what in the MSA.
[00:34] Priya: I can cover the tech tradeoffs briefly — when customers choose Redwood Dedicated we provide reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput, and we can enable a private control plane for VPC/on-prem deployments — apologies if I mangle the product names, our internal sometimes says Redwood Dedi or Redwood Private.
[00:51] Ravi: Quick question on data flow: for Dedicated with VPC routing, does customer traffic ever transit Redwood-managed storage or is it all within the VPC? Also KMS integration — we have a corporate HSM provider.
[01:05] Marcus: Good questions. For Private/VPC mode the control plane can be customer-managed and data plane traffic stays in your VPC; logs and metrics can be configured to forward to your S3 or account logging bucket. For KMS, we support external KMS/HSM integration — need to verify the exact vendor connectors but generally we do bring-your-own-key.
[01:30] Sofia: On the DPA, Orchid's standard requires data residency for EU PII and a right to audit. Are you able to support contract language around audit access and subprocessor lists?
[01:45] Priya: We maintain a subprocessor list and SOC2 artifacts; for audits we typically provide attestation reports and can coordinate a narrow-scope audit for enterprise tiers. Marcus, do you want to add on the legal side?
[01:58] Marcus: Sure — for SOC2/ISO we can provide reports under NDA. Regarding DPAs, our standard DPA covers data residency options and subprocessors; we understand customers sometimes need tighter language, so Orchid's legal can redline and we'll follow up. Typical timeline for MSA/DPA negotiation is 2–4 weeks for medium complexity; longer if there are bespoke audit terms.
[02:15] David: That's reasonable. For SLAs, we need 99.9% uptime and P95 latency under 200ms for our gen workloads. Does Redwood commit to that on hosted or do for Dedicated?
[02:30] Priya: 99.9% is within the realms of Dedicated SLA depending on region and instance families, but latency guarantees depend on model, sequence length, and batching. P95 200ms is aggressive for large models at moderate token counts; we'd need to check model family and token budget. We can run focused 95th-percentile tests on a dedicated node type to validate.
[02:55] Emily: From procurement's view we just need to know if that SLA is something we'll get in writing and what credits look like. Also pricing tiers for dedicated pool sizes.
[03:07] Marcus: We do offer SLA-backed uptime for Dedicated with credits for breaches; the credit mechanism will be in the SLA section of the MSA and is negotiable based on commitment. Pricing tiers depend on reserved vGPU hours and whether you want burst capacity. I'll share the pricing matrix after this call.
[03:26] Ravi: Encryption in transit and at rest — is the data encrypted by default? Also how long are logs retained and can we disable certain logs for PII?
[03:36] Priya: Data at rest is encrypted; in transit uses TLS. Log retention is configurable — we can set short retention for request traces and you can opt out of storing payloads in logs. We'll need to map exactly which logs Orchid wants retained.
[03:52] Sofia: For the DPA there are a few clauses we almost never accept — unlimited subprocessor disclosure, broad right-to-audit with no scope, and open-ended indemnities. We'll mark those for redline.
[04:05] Marcus: Understood. If you send the standard redline we'll review and respond; we try to keep indemnities reciprocal and limits reasonable.
[04:12] David: Timeline wise, procurement wants signatures by mid-October if possible. We have a budget cycle that closes 10/20. Is that feasible?
[04:20] Marcus: If redlines are simple and we can agree on an initial Dedicated config, mid-October is feasible. We'll need the approvals and purchase order.
[04:27] Emily: Also do you have a standard SOW for proof of concept? We often start POCs to validate latency and cost before full commit.
[04:34] Priya: Yes, we can run a 4-week POC with a scoped SOW that includes acceptance criteria (latency buckets, throughput). We usually provide a reduced-price POC with access to Dedicated pool on a limited basis. Priya: Based on the POC results we provide recommendations — batching configs, quantization suggestions, and caching knobs to hit cost/latency targets.
[04:55] David: That would help with internal signoff. On pricing approvals, what is the procurement flow? Do you need a signed MSA before onboarding or can MSA and SOW be parallel?
[05:08] Marcus: We prefer MSA signed before SOW kick-off, but for velocity we can provision a scoped onboarding under a mutual NDA and then exchange MSA redlines in parallel. Emily: That flexibility helps.
[05:21] Ravi: A technical follow-up — priya mentioned KV cash earlier, did you say KV cache? (laughter)
[05:27] Priya: KV cache, yes sorry, my slip. We do prefix/KV caching to reduce repeated token costs. We'll document how that impacts throughput.
[05:40] Sofia: Data residency — some of our EU customers cannot have model outputs stored outside EU. Do you offer regionally pinned deployments?
[05:50] Marcus: Yes we have region-pinned Dedicated and Private options. For strict residency you can run the Private bundle in your VPC or on-prem, depending on compliance.
[06:00] David: Can you give an example of a pricing band for 10M tokens/month for Dedicated vs Hosted? I know it's approximate but we need order-of-magnitude for budget.
[06:12] Marcus: I'll send a compact TCO spreadsheet but roughly Dedicated with a medium reserved pool could be 20–40% cheaper at scale versus hosted, depending on batching and cache hit rates. Exact numbers depend on model, sequence length, and utilization.
[06:30] Emily: For procurement we also need vendor risk questionnaire answers and subprocessor list. Do you have a centralized place for that?
[06:38] Marcus: Yes, we have a vendor questionnaire pack and a subprocessors list PDF. I'll share a secure link.
[06:45] Ravi: About the SOC2 — is it in-scope for the product? We need the Type II report.
[06:52] Marcus: We can provide SOC2 Type II under an NDA. Also ISO 27001 summary if helpful.
[07:00] Sofia: If we redline the DPA with some of our stricter audit wording, is Redwood open to a specific narrow-scope audit rather than broad rights?
[07:10] Marcus: Yes, we can entertain a scoped audit with pre-agreed SOW and timing. That would likely be part of an enterprise contract.
[07:18] David: Okay. Let's talk about decision makers — who at Orchid needs to sign? Procurement, legal, and a final exec approval. Timeline tentatively mid-October.
[07:27] Emily: Yes procurement will need the pricing and the PO; legal will handle the redlines.
[07:33] Priya: Tech team involvement — we should run a short benchmark. Can you share a representative prompt set and expected token lengths?
[07:42] David: We'll share a set from our customer support pipeline and a couple of high-length examples. Expect variable sequences up to about 1k tokens but most are 150–250.
[07:55] Priya: That's helpful. For 150–250 tokens P95 200ms might be achievable with a smaller model family or tuned batching; for 1k tokens it's much harder. We'll run targeted tests on the Dedicated node.
[08:10] Emily: On the MSA, are there any indemnity clauses we need to be aware of on your side? Our legal will push back on open-ended indemnity.
[08:20] Marcus: Our standard has mutual indemnities with caps tied to fees; we'll share the template.
[08:27] Sofia: Also need to confirm data deletion terms — can you support deletion of payloads on request with audit trail?
[08:34] Priya: Yes, we support data deletion APIs and can provide confirmation logs. We'll outline retention windows and deletion mechanics in the DPA appendix.
[08:46] Marcus: Quick note: we also have a dedicated onboarding doc for private deployments that covers IP, network ACLs, and certificate rotation. I'll attach that.
[08:55] David: Sounds good. For next steps can we recap who does what and when?
[09:00] Marcus: Sure — action items: Marcus will share MSA + DPA examples, pricing tiers, and the vendor questionnaire by Friday (2025-10-03). Priya will run latency benchmarks and provide a compact TCO by 2025-10-06. Orchid will provide sample prompt set and KMS vendor info by 2025-10-02. Legal will complete initial DPA redlines within the week.
[09:22] Emily: One more procurement question — payment terms and billing cadence? We prefer net-45 on PO with milestone billing. Is that acceptable?
[09:30] Marcus: Payment terms can be negotiated; standard is net-30 but enterprise customers can request net-45 with purchase orders and multi-year commitments. I'll flag that.
[09:40] Ravi: Security follow-up: we'll want a short technical workshop to map KMS flows, key rotation, and log sanitization. Can Priya lead that?
[09:48] Priya: Yes, happy to run a 60-minute deep dive.
[09:52] Sofia: And legal will attach a list of non-starters in the redline — things like audit scope and indemnity caps.
[09:59] Marcus: Perfect. Anything else?
[10:03] David: No, that's all. Appreciate the clarity.
[10:07] Marcus: Great thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and schedule the SE workshop.
[10:12] Emily: Thanks.
[10:15] End of recording.
